1.  **Engine Modification (Prerequisite):** Modify the UE5 source code to change signed 32-bit integer (`int32`) types to unsigned 32-bit (`uint32`) or 64-bit (`int64`) in SVT import and resource handling code. [S1, S2, unofficial]

The claim states that evidence supports modifying UE5 source code to change signed 32-bit integers (int32) to unsigned 32-bit (uint32) or 64-bit (int64) in SVT import and resource handling code. Both Source [S1] and Source [S2] explicitly confirm this. S1 notes that 'Initial implementation of SVT in UE5 suffered from signed 32-bit integer (int32) overflows... Fix the integer overflow issue by modifying the UE5 source code to change problematic int32 types to uint32 or int64'. S2 corroborates this, stating 'We found at least two places in the source code that caused an overﬂow at 2 gigabyte data size, due to signed int32 usage. Our ﬁxes allowed us to extend the importing capabilities...'. The claim accurately reflects the facts presented in the evidence.

Sparse Volume Texture Setup is a method for importing and configuring large, sparse volumetric datasets (up to ~6 gigavoxels) into Unreal Engine 5 using Sparse Volume Textures (SVT) [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial][S3].

The claim states that Sparse Volume Texture Setup is a method for importing and configuring large, sparse volumetric datasets (up to ~6 gigavoxels) into Unreal Engine 5 using Sparse Volume Textures (SVT). Source [S1] confirms that the modified SVT approach allows rendering sparse datasets up to 32k x 32k x 16k voxels (which exceeds 6 gigavoxels in total volume, though practical compressed data limits are noted around 4-6 gigavoxels depending on padding/mipmaps) and specifically mentions the successful import and rendering of the 6 billion voxel Kolumbo dataset. Source [S2] explicitly states that the modified engine enables rendering a sparse dataset of 5.9 gigavoxels (approx ~6 gigavoxels) and discusses the import process and configuration (console commands, material parameters). Source [S3] details the setup and configuration aspects (UV coordinates, material nodes). All specific facts in the claim (method name, purpose, engine version, technology, and size limit) are supported by the provided evidence.

*   **Strengths:** Seamless rendering of full datasets without chunking artifacts; supports full lighting, emission, and color; interactive exploration via MPC/DMI [S1, S2, unofficial].

The evidence in Source [S1] and Source [S2] explicitly supports all components of the claim: 1) 'Seamless rendering of full datasets without chunking artifacts' is confirmed by statements that the modified approach renders the full dataset without chunking, unlike TBRayMarcher or Niagara which require chunking and suffer from artifacts. 2) 'Supports full lighting, emission, and color' is supported by mentions of the material system allowing runtime manipulation of density, emission, color maps, and receiving lighting from arbitrary lights. 3) 'Interactive exploration via MPC/DMI' is directly supported by passages stating that interactive exploration features are made available via Material Parameter Collections (MPC) and Dynamic Material Instances (DMI).
